title: Scientists discover breakthrough new way to find alien life with AI | The Independent
body:
The work is reported in a new paper, ‘Chiral discrimination of amino acids in meteorite and desert soil extracts via single-molecule nanogap conductance’, published in the journal Nature Communications.

## Join our commenting forum

Join thought-provoking conversations, follow other Independent readers and see their replies

Comments [...] In the new study, the scientists were able to measure molecules as they passed through a gap between two extremely thin pieces of gold wire. The waveforms of the current as it passes between those wires is different depending on which kind of amino acid is there, and so the equipment makes it possible to tell them apart by counting the molecules as they pass. [...] “By combining our nanogap tunneling technique with artificial intelligence, we were able to distinguish between the L- and D-forms of amino acids with over 80 per cent accuracy,” said lead author, Takahito Oshiro. “This is the first discrimination of amino-acid chirality at the single-molecule level and constitutes a fundamental advance in chemical sensing.”

body: This launch comes as Intel attempts to establish a more competitive position in AI acceleration following its previous Gaudi efforts that were well-regarded but not very popular. This is a powerful inference-focused accelerator built around the new Xe3P architecture, supposedly the 'full' version of the Xe3 architecture that debuted with Panther Lake. The card combines up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory with 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8 compute in [...] Intel says customer sampling is already underway and that it is working with OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers, and software partners to bring the hardware to market. title: New cyber threat to water systems exposes limits of encryption
body:
Industrial control systems rely on computers to run physical machinery such as pumps, valves and generators. Unlike attacks that compromise equipment inside a plant or overwhelm a network with traffic, the new technique uses patterns in encrypted communications to predict critical moments and selectively block a small fraction of messages.

This allows the attack to disrupt operations without entering the plant's own systems while evading the attack detectors tested by the researchers. [...] The technique targets facilities that communicate with cloud-based monitoring and control systems over encrypted connections. title: Ransomware Groups Increasingly Resorting to Real World Threats
body: Ransomware groups have responded by adopting more aggressive tactics, and a trend has emerged of ransomware groups issuing personal threats against company employees and their friends and family members. The survey revealed that 37% of ransomware attacks involved threats against friends or family members of staff members, and 41% of respondents to the survey said they had been a target of physical or psychological intimidation. [...] The threat of data erasure, destruction, and publication remains the most common tactic (56%), followed by blackmail/extortion (41%), and system lockouts or sabotage (40%); however, 23% of malicious actors have resorted to psychological intimidation, 17% are issuing physical threats, and in 10% of cases, have threatened legal exposure. Semperis warns in its third annual ransomware report that personal threats are gaining more traction. Out of the individuals who received personal threats, 57% [...] While contacting individuals whose data was stolen in an attack has been adopted by several groups in the past, the threats have generally been limited to the publication of personal data, but threats are becoming more severe. Ransomware groups are now issuing threats of physical violence and are contacting employees and their friends and family members via text, email, or phone, confirming that they know where they live, work, and even where their children go to school.
